To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Images of self vulnerability and self capability affect the images of opportunity that underlie opportunity identification; (2) Images of self capability are more important in the identification of entrepreneurial opportunities than are images of self vulnerability; and (3) The effect of images of self capability on the images of opportunity underlying opportunity identification is mediated by the degree to which an individual is willing to take risks.
images of capability positively impact the images of opportunities, and images of vulnerability negatively impact the images of opportunity.
images of self vulnerability (images of self capability) lead to images of opportunity that are more (less) uncertain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of images of self in the entrepreneurial opportunity recognition process.
the relationship between images of self and opportunity recognition.
the role of the self in opportunity recognition, but we focus on the images of self that entrepreneurs bring to the process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

entrepreneurs' images of self vulnerability are positively related to the perceived feasibility of the opportunity and that images of self capability are positively related to both the perceived feasibility and the attractiveness of the opportunity.
the images of self vulnerability (or images of capability) are positively (negatively) related to images of opportunity vulnerability (capability).
entrepreneurs who are more capable are less likely to perceive an opportunity as being attractive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the images of self that individuals hold affect how they perceive opportunities and, thus, the likelihood they will recognize opportunities.
the images of self that entrepreneurs have influence the images of opportunity that they form and thus their decisions about opportunities.
images of self vulnerability increase the perceived risk of an opportunity while images of capability increase the perceived potential of an opportunity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
images of vulnerability and capability are important for opportunity recognition.
the self is not a monolithic construct, and that different images of self may lead individuals to different interpretations of the same opportunity.
